changes.text: 1768年6月中旬，叫魂的谣言从浙江传进了江西。它走的是江西东面的信江河谷，那是通往邻省浙江的一条便捷通道。江西巡抚吴绍诗年约七十。谣言已经进了他的辖境，他没有向朝廷奏报。

In the middle of June 1768, rumours of soulstealing crossed from Zhejiang into Jiangxi. They came through the Xin River valley on Jiangxi's eastern side, the easy route into the neighbouring province. The governor of Jiangxi, Wu Shaoshi, was about seventy. The rumours had entered his jurisdiction, and he sent no report to the court.
这一年，乾隆皇帝弘历追究各地官员为何抓不到妖党首犯。研究这场风波的历史学家孔飞力指出，皇帝的怒气可以发在没抓到首犯的地方官身上，而这种失职躲不开，因为这样的妖首并不存在。孔飞力也强调，弘历当时并没有察觉这个案子的荒谬。巡抚们面对的，是一位认真追究的皇帝，和一个抓不到的目标。

That year the Qianlong emperor, Hongli, pressed provincial officials over their failure to catch the sorcerers' leaders. Philip A. Kuhn, the historian who reconstructed the panic, points out that the emperor could turn his anger on provincial officials who failed to catch those leaders. They could not avoid failing, because no such leader existed. Kuhn also insists that Hongli did not see the absurdity of the case at the time. The governors faced an emperor who meant every word of his orders, and a quarry that could not be caught.
先看邻省的巡抚是怎么回话的。河南巡抚阿思哈向弘历解释，术士们有隐身的秘术，所以逃脱了。弘历在朱批里嘲笑他：你心里存着这种想法，难怪属下缉拿不力，他们是在欺你这个「无用废物」。替抓不到人找理由，换来的是皇帝的嘲骂。

Consider first how governors elsewhere answered. Asiha, the governor of Henan, explained to Hongli that the sorcerers had escaped because they knew a secret art of making themselves invisible. Hongli answered in a rescript, the comment the emperor wrote in vermilion ink on an official's report. He mocked Asiha: with ideas like that in his head, no wonder his subordinates were slack about arrests, since they were taking him for a "useless good-for-nothing." Offering an excuse for catching no one only brought the emperor's ridicule.
此外，弘历对吴绍诗的家族也十分尊重：吴绍诗是一个著名法律世家的大家长。按照回避原则，同一家族的成员通常不许同时在这样的衙门任职，但吴绍诗和他的儿子吴焕、吴坛，曾两次被同时任命在刑部供职。

Hongli also held Wu Shaoshi's family in high regard. Wu Shaoshi headed a celebrated family of legal experts. Under the rule of avoidance, members of one family were normally barred from serving in the same government office at the same time. Even so, Wu Shaoshi and his sons Wu Huan and Wu Tan were twice appointed together to the Board of Punishments, the central ministry of justice.

吴绍诗的次子吴坛是邻省江苏的按察使，和父亲一样是受人尊敬的法律学者。他的情形与父亲不同：他没有向朝廷报告的，是江苏当年春天实际发生的叫魂案件。织造萨载把叫魂案密报上去，吴坛因此蒙羞。吴坛承认自己未及时报告，弘历在朱批里先提他过去的表现：「汝在刑部时，表现出色。然一任外省，即染模棱腐败之陋习。」意思是你在刑部时干得很好，一到地方就染上了含糊敷衍、腐败的毛病。最后骂他是「不知恩之物」，不知感恩的东西。父亲得到一句「汝误矣」，儿子挨了一通痛骂。

Wu Shaoshi's second son, Wu Tan, was judicial commissioner of neighbouring Jiangsu. Like his father he was a respected legal scholar. His case was different, though: what he failed to report to the court were actual soulstealing cases in Jiangsu that spring. Then Sazai, the imperial textile commissioner, sent a secret report on the cases, and Wu Tan was disgraced. When Wu Tan admitted that he had failed to report in time, Hongli's rescript began with his past record: "When you were at the Board of Punishments, you performed splendidly. But as soon as you took a provincial post, you caught the vile habits of equivocation and corruption." It ended by calling him an "ungrateful creature." The father received "You were wrong" and the son a torrent of abuse.

报告里还有一段警告。他说那些从事「左道邪术」的人，借创立烧香好善会的名义，「阳则聚集乡愚男妇，阴则勾结亡命棍徒」，明面上聚集乡间男女，暗地里勾结亡命之徒；又借避灾防盗之名，造作妖言、制备军器、诱人归附。他要求不论僧道还是其他人，凡是面生可疑、神气沮丧、迁徙无定、怕见人的，都要立即报告地方官。弘历的朱批是：「恐属空言，实难信矣口」，恐怕只是空话，实在难以相信。这是一句明白的怀疑，针对的正是这份奏报。

The report also carried a warning. Practitioners of "heterodox ways and evil arts," it said, set up incense-burning charitable societies as a front, "openly gathering ignorant village men and women, secretly colluding with desperadoes and ruffians." On the pretext of warding off disaster and bandits, they spread wicked talk, stockpiled weapons and drew people into their following. Wu Shaoshi ordered that anyone, monk, Daoist priest or layman, who was an unfamiliar face, looked dejected, kept moving from place to place, or avoided being seen, be reported to the local officials at once. Hongli's rescript read: "I fear these are empty words; truly hard to believe." It was open doubt, aimed squarely at this report.

吴坛走的是另一条路。挨骂大约三个星期后，约9月28日，他奏报说，虽然没有抓到叫魂案犯，但查访发现苏州城外有十一座由俗人建造的佛教经堂。随后约七十人被他逮捕，供词显示这些教派从1677年起就在当地活动。孔飞力自己说明无法证实，但他推测：这种规模的教派在苏州这样繁忙的城市不可能长期瞒过官府；按察使受到抓人的压力，压向属下，底层经办人员便拿这些无事而易欺的信徒来交差。弘历的反应十分严厉，下令严惩这些教徒，并审问他们与叫魂案的联系。经堂案又牵出一轮追责，受罚名单从知县一直排到总督，但大多数人只受到象征性处罚，孔飞力称之为一幕闹剧。

Wu Tan went another way. Around September 28, about three weeks after the emperor's tirade, he reported that he had caught no soulstealers, but his inquiries had uncovered eleven Buddhist scripture halls outside Suzhou, built by lay believers. He then arrested about seventy people, and their confessions showed that the sects had been active in the area since 1677. Kuhn says plainly that he cannot prove it, but he conjectures that sects of this size could not have stayed hidden from the authorities for long in a city as busy as Suzhou. In his reading, the judicial commissioner was under pressure to make arrests and passed it down to his subordinates, and the clerks and runners at the bottom handed over these harmless, easily bullied believers to have something to show for their efforts. Hongli reacted very severely. He ordered the sectarians harshly punished and had them questioned about any links to the soulstealing. The scripture-hall case then set off a round of punishments for past officials, with names ranging from county magistrates up to governors-general, though most received only token penalties. Kuhn calls the impeachment process a farce.
江西到底发生了什么？孔飞力摆出两种可能：要么这张警网从来没有真正动用过，要么它根本捕捉不到嫌犯。他注意到，江西看不到其他省份那种刑求和伪证，于是推断吴绍诗根本不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子，那些忧心忡忡的警告和精心的布置都只是「装模作样」。这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载；他先列出过警网根本捕捉不到嫌犯的可能，但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信前一种。

What actually happened in Jiangxi? Kuhn sets out two possibilities: either the net was never really put to use, or it was incapable of catching anyone. He observes that Jiangxi shows none of the torture and false testimony found in other provinces, and from this he concludes that Wu Shaoshi never intended to pursue a case he believed rested on false rumour. In Kuhn's view, the anxious warnings and the elaborate deployment were only a performance. That is Kuhn's inference, not something the archives record. He first named the possibility that the net could not catch anyone, but on the absence of torture and false testimony concluded that only the first explanation was credible.

这也不是一个智者对抗暴君的故事。孔飞力列举过官僚抵制的几种情形：有深思熟虑的，有程序颟顸误了时机的，有因不信其事而轻视此案的，有怕清剿危及仕途的，也可能有耿直官员拒绝依据诬告迫害无辜。他说这些行动不像是协调一致的，抵制专制权力并不需要串通。本文无法据此判定吴绍诗属于哪一种。孔飞力也提醒，说弘历“利用”了政治罪，并不比说政治罪“利用”了他更接近真实。本文作者的一种解读是，江西的平静和苏州的七十人被捕，都出自同一套结构，差别在于每个官员怎样接住同一份压力。

Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Some came from sluggish procedures that kept officials from reacting to an emergency in time. Some officials, doubting the whole thing, may have refused to take the cases seriously. Others may have feared that a purge would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. This article cannot say which of these describes Wu Shaoshi. Kuhn also cautions that saying Hongli "used" political crime is no closer to the truth than saying political crime "used" him. My own reading is that the quiet in Jiangxi and the seventy arrests in Suzhou came out of the same structure. What differed was how each official handled the same pressure.
本文唯一的依据是孔飞力《叫魂》的中译本（陈兼、刘昶译），没有使用其他史源。朱批和奏报都转引自书中译文，与档案原文是否逐字一致无法判断。“只是装模作样”是孔飞力的推断，他先列出过警网根本抓不到人的可能，但倾向于装模作样的解释；吴绍诗为何难以受罚，孔飞力归于他的法律造诣，并推测可能还有高晋的袒护。高晋答应的后续报告，孔飞力没有找到。

This article rests entirely on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers, by Chen Jian and Liu Chang, and uses no other source. The rescripts and memorials are quoted as they appear in that translation, so I cannot tell whether they match the archival originals word for word, and the English renderings here are translations of that Chinese text. The claim that Wu Shaoshi was merely putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Kuhn first named the possibility that the net simply could not catch anyone, but leaned toward the explanation that it was a show. As for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Kuhn attributes it to his legal expertise and conjectures that Gao Jin's protection may also have played a part. Kuhn was unable to find the follow-up report Gao Jin promised.
本文只依据孔飞力《叫魂》中译本。朱批引文照书中原样，「恐属空言，实难信矣口」中的“口”字照录未改。吴绍诗“装模作样”是孔飞力的推断；他为何难以受罚，孔飞力给出的理由中，高晋的袒护一项是推测。

This article relies only on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers. Rescripts are rendered from the text as printed there. In that text, the rescript translated here as "I fear these are empty words; truly hard to believe" ends with a stray character (口) that the Chinese article reproduces unchanged, and it is left out of the English translation. The view that Wu Shaoshi was only putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Of the reasons Kuhn gives for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Gao Jin's protection is a conjecture.
